title: Heterometallic [Mn5Ln4] Single-Molecule Magnets with High Anisotropy Barriers

synthesis.procedure: Prepared analogously to 3: Tb(NO3)3·6H2O was added to a stirred slurry of [Mn6O2(Piv)10(4-Me-py)2.5(PivH)1.5] (1) and N-methyldiethanolamine in MeCN. After stirring 5 min at room temperature, the mixture was heated under reflux for 40 min to give a dark brown solution, cooled, filtered, and left to evaporate slowly at room temperature. Brown crystals formed after two weeks, were collected by filtration, washed with cold MeCN, and dried in air.

properties.summary: Isostructural Mn5Tb4 SMM. Room-temperature χT is 67.8 cm3 K mol−1 (1000 Oe). Frequency-dependent ac out-of-phase signals give Arrhenius parameters Δeff = 33 K and τ0 = 4.5×10−9 s. Slow relaxation is observed above 1.8 K; below about 2 K the relaxation time departs from Arrhenius behaviour, indicating quantum tunnelling.

synthesis.procedure: Dy(NO3)3·6H2O (0.30 g, 0.66 mmol) was added to a stirred slurry of 1 (0.20 g, 0.11 mmol) and N-methyldiethanolamine (0.147 g, 1.23 mmol) in MeCN (15 mL). After stirring for 5 min at room temperature, the mixture was heated under reflux for 40 min to give a dark brown solution. The solution was allowed to cool, filtered, and left to evaporate slowly at room temperature. Brown crystals were obtained after two weeks, collected by filtration, washed with cold MeCN (5 mL), and dried in air.

properties.summary: Mn5Dy4 SMM with the highest energy barrier then reported for a 3d–4f SMM. χT is 62.2 cm3 K mol−1 at room temperature, decreases to 50.2 at ~17 K, rises to 62.4 at 4.5 K, then drops to 54.4 at 1.8 K (1000 Oe). Arrhenius parameters from ac/dc relaxation data are Δeff = 38.6 K and τ0 = 3.0×10−9 s. Single-crystal m-SQUID hysteresis loops appear below 1.9 K (0.002 T s−1); coercive field reaches about 1 T at 0.4 K, with QTM-dominated, sweep-rate-dependent magnetisation below that temperature.

properties.summary: Mn5Ho4 analogue shows SMM-like frequency-dependent ac signals but no χ″ maximum above 1.8 K even at 1500 Hz, so a barrier could not be fitted; the ac response resembles 5 and suggests an energy gap around 20 K. Room-temperature χT is 60.9 cm3 K mol−1, rising to a maximum of 73.4 cm3 K mol−1 at 3 K, consistent with a large-spin ground state. Applied dc fields do not slow the relaxation, implying weak quantum-tunnelling influence in the studied range and only a weak Ho contribution to the anisotropy.

properties.summary: Diamagnetic YIII analogue used to isolate the MnIII4MnIV magnetism. Room-temperature χT is 10.5 cm3 K mol−1 and falls to 1.8 cm3 K mol−1 at 1.8 K (0.1 T). Heisenberg fit above 10 K gives J1/kB = −45(2) K, J2/kB = +6.0(5) K, J3/kB = −9.0(5) K, g = 2.1(1), and an ST = 3/2 ground state. Zero-field ac χ″ is weak and noisy; under an optimum 4500 Oe dc field the energy gap is 20.2 K with τ0 = 2.6×10−8 s.
